text:
sarah: Quick question — we have a docs-only PR that needs to go in during the change window tonight. Can we rollforward without bumping the patch? releasebot currently forces a patch.
releasebot: FYI: current behavior — any merge to main triggers releasebot patch-bump unless PR has label 'chore:skip-release' or files are under infra/only. No docs-only heuristic today.
alex: I think docs-only should be safe to skip. Lots of users pin to semver but docs don't affect runtime.
jorge: Agree in principle but caveat — some downstream consumers pin to exact patch numbers and expect changelog entries. If we skip bump, they won't see an update and may be confused.
priya: Also thinking of rollback tooling — we rely on consistent tag names for automated rollbacks. If we don't create a new tag, rollback scripts might behave oddly.
alex: What if releasebot supports a 'skip-patch' label that still creates a metadata-only record (so rollback tooling can reference a record) but doesn't increment the visible semver? e.g., create an internal meta tag like meta/sha-<short> and attach changelog note.
jorge: That could work. Alternative: detect docs-only by diff, e.g.:
```
CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only $BASE..HEAD)
if echo "$CHANGED" | grep -qvE "^docs/|^README.md"; then \ 
  # not docs-only
fi
```
But detection edge-cases exist (generated files, example configs).
sarah: I like the 'meta tag' compromise because it preserves an audit trail without bumping the public version. But we need the release notes and a clear signal in the changelog ("docs-only: no semver bump").
priya: Ops concern: our release dashboard and billing rely on tag-based artifacts. If releasebot omits a tag, some dashboards will show mismatched data. So either create a lightweight tag or ensure dashboards ignore meta-only merges.
alex: Implementation plan I propose: 1) add label 'skip-patch' recognized by releasebot; 2) releasebot checks diff whitelist (docs/, .md, assets/docs) as fallback; 3) on skip, releasebot creates a meta tag `meta/<short-sha>` and posts a release note entry flagged docs-only; 4) gating: only allowed during non-emergency windows and requires at least one docs-team approver.
jorge: +1 but add a safety net: if downstream consumers have pinned to exact tag in last 30 days, block skip and force bump. We can query usage metrics before deciding.
releasebot: noted — can implement the label & meta tag flow. Will default to 'force bump' if any binary/compiled files detected. Also can add a config flag per repo: releasebot.skip_patch_enabled = true/false.
sarah: Ok sounds good. Action items: alex -> open PR to releasebot with label + meta tag logic; priya -> write short ops note about rollback/dashboard implications; jorge -> run quick scan for consumers pinned to exact patches and report back; i'll update changelog template to render docs-only entries clearly.
alex: on it, opening PR this morning :thumbsup:
priya: I'll draft the ops note and ping infra for dashboard changes.
jorge: I'll run the pinning check and post results before EOD.
releasebot: Test run queued on staging for the new flow. Use `releasebot test --repo redwood/api --branch docs-sans-bump` to exercise.
sarah: Thanks — if everything's green we'll use the skip flow for tonight's docs rollforward.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled for 22:00 UTC.
alex: ack — will monitor.
priya: ack.
jorge: ack.
